SUBSCRIPTION PRICE 2 TWENTY-FIVE CENTS 


OPENING MESSAGE FOR ASSOCIATION YEAR 
BEGINNING MAY 1, 1919 


By Mr. A. O. Dawson, VicE-PRESIDENT 


THE season of the year has again arrived when the officers and 

members of the Young Men’s Christian Association are called 
upon to review the work of the past twelve months, and to make 
preparations for the year that is before us. 

While all our expectations have not been realized yet, we are 
constrained to thank God for the many men, both soldiers and 
civilians, whose lives have been enriched through having come in 
touch with this great organization. 

The service thus rendered would have been greatly restricted 
had it not been for the unselfish and most valued assistance of many 
devoted Christian ladies who were ready to respond to the many 
calls made upon them. 

Surely, in these days of unrest, there is a special need that Chris- 
tian men shall take their proper place in leadership, and prove by 
both precept and example that the only real solution of the problems 
that press upon us must be found in the Man Christ Jesus. More 
than ever He must be the source and centre of all our effort. He 
only can satisfy our aspirations and desires, and therefore it must 
be our chief business to introduce Him to our young men. ‘This 
must be our objective through every agency—Physical, Mental and 
Spiritual. 

The year before us will bring us that measure of success accord- 
ing to the loyalty shown to our Master and Lord. Sin is the disturb- 
ing factor in society to-day, and sin can only be removed through 
that One from whom our organization has taken its name. 

The unconquerable love of God that even our sin cannot quench 
is what we must tell our men about. ‘The world unrest is the cry of 
man for his God even though he may not be conscious of his need. 
Let us then tell these men by word and act that God satisfies, that 
He meets law with justification, the breach of love with forgiveness, 
loneliness with fellowship, defilement with purity, weakness with 
power, and fear with hope. 


2 MONTREAL MEN 


Sixty~Eight Annnal Report 


OF THE 


YOUNG MEN’S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION 
OF THE CITY OF MONTREAL 
YEAR ENDED APRIL 30th, 1919 


[': is beyond our power to estimate the results obtained from this 

year’s Association work. Many have been the opportunities 
presented to us, and in our efforts to meet these opportunities we 
gratefully acknowledge the guiding hand of God. 

The greatest war known to man reached its climax and its close 
on, the battle plains of Europe during this year. Such awful clash 
of arms and destruction of human life has never been known before, 
and we earnestly hope may never be known again. 

Our Canadian Association took its place by the side of the soldier, 
serving its King and Country in the front line and communicating 
trenches; establishing Red Triangle dugouts and canteen: booths on 
the way up to the front; distributing comforts to the soldiers in many 
forms and aiding materially the morale of the troops; serving buns, 
coffee and other comforts to the walking wounded as they passed 
on their way back after an engagement with the enemy; supplying 
for the soldiers when resting, religious services, cinemas, concerts 
and entertainments and games, so necessary to break the awful 
nightmare of war; and providing the material and encouraging the 
soldiers to write to mother, sister, sweetheart and friend. Such 
have been the activities of our Canadian Association overseas. 

The Association in our City has served the soldiers in its four 
buildings, in the Red Triangle Hut and at the Turcot Yards. Over 
6,000 free memberships have been issued since the beginning of the 
war. The Red Triangle Hut has served 20,000 meals per month. 
Their full dormitory capacity since the beginning of the year has 
been taxed to its limit. A programme suitable to the returned man, 
providing entertainment, education and exercise, has been put on. 
The “Tuck Shop” and the Canteen have been patronized extensively 
by the soldiers. One day’s free meals and lodging is given each man 
upon his arrival in the City, and this has proved a great boon to the 
soldiers. 

Since the beginning of the war there have enlisted from our 
membership over 2,500 men. Of these tor have paid the supreme 
price. It is with reverence that we remind ourselves of the place 
they. hold in our affection and pray that the great example of their 
sacrifice shall stimulate the membership of our Montreal Association 
to increased earnestness in work for the Master. 

Rexicious Work. 
The religious work of the Association this year has been to 
emphasize Bible Study more than in other years. Our Vice-Presi- 


dent, Mr. A. O. Dawson, and the Rev. Harold Young, M.A., 


MONTREAL MEN 3 


associate pastor of St. James Methodist Church, with other 
leaders, conducted Bible Classes in Central Branch every Thursday 
evening, which have been well attended. Many similar classes have 
also been held in the other Branches. Short term courses in Bible 
Study and Life Problems were well attended and splendid results 
obtained. 

Plans for starting fourteen Bible Study Groups were fully matured 
during the first part of October last year when the influenza appeared 
and activities in the Branches were entirely suspended. Central 
Branch was closed from October 8 to November 11, and the other 
Branches in the City closed for an equal length of time. This mate- 
rially curtailed the work we had in mind, but, notwithstanding this, 
we were able to carry through a more aggressive religious work 
programme. 

The physical and social activities in all the branches have been 
well maintained, although seriously interrupted during the epidemic 
last Fall. 

A special request has come from Central Branch urging that your 
Directors take steps at once to secure suitable grounds for outdoor 
athletics. The need of a centrally located track and grounds is keenly 
felt when our Physical Directors are planning their summer pro- 
gramme. 


Your Board of Directors were seized with the responsibility 
thrust upon them by the return of the soldiers, and the great need 
of extending the work of the Association to cover every section of 
the City. With that in view, the Community Committee were 
requested to study the whole situation and bring in a report which 
would be considered at a special meeting of the Board. 


This report was adopted as a basis for a ten-year programme and 
an extension of our work into the industrial field, placing a Secretary, 
where possible, in each of our large industrial plants; also placing a 
Secretary in each section of the City not yet served as rapidly as 
properly trained men can be secured. 

Mr. G. D. Brandon, on the 1st of May this year, joined the 
Metropolitan staff as Community Secretary for Point St. Charles 
and Verdun. It is the desire of the Board in the near future to supply 
the need of a man in St. Lambert and in Maisonneuve, who will co- 
operate with the churches and other agencies there in a community 
type of work. 

The Sixth Annual Report of the Community Committee has 
been filed. This touches on the extended activities of the Associa- 
tion and its co-operation with other organizations, such as organiza- 
tions for work with boys, Social Workers’ Federation, foreign speak- 
ing peoples, co-operation with McGill, sex education, Training 
School, co-operation with the Y.W.C.A., Story Tellers’ League, 
Sunday School Association, Committee of Sixteen, National Council. 

Our Community Secretary is rendering a wide service to the reli- 
gious and social forces of the City. 


4 MONTREAL MEN 


FINANCIAL. 

In the Red Triangle Financial Campaign in May, 1918, our local 
budget of $40,000 was provided. Your Finance Committee are 
pleased to be able to pert that they have lived within their budget. 
Our Railroad Branch did not require the full amount they requested 
in their budget, but the amounts asked for by Central, North End 
and Westmount had to be supplemented. This was made necessary 
owing to extensive repairs to the buildings, which had not been done 
over since the buildings were erected in 1912. 


We have distributed to the Branches, this year, $29,570, as 
compared with $17,315.78 in 1917-18. 
The following legacies have been received during the year:—

Your Directors and Committees of Management of the different 
branches, as in other years, have carefully checked and audited all 
expenditures and improvements before same were authorized, real- 
izing that in this strenuous war period the greatest economy and 
husbanding of our finances were absolutely necessary. 


Camps 


The Senior anal was open for two weeks—July 13 to 29, 
1918—with Mr. W. H. Henderson and Mr. W. A. MacLaren in 
charge; also during week-ends and holidays in May, June and 
August, with an attendance of seventy-two members. ‘The enlist- 
ment for overseas’ service from our membership greatly interfered 
with the operation of the Senior Camp this year. The financial 
statement shows a balance of $73 on the right side. 


Our Junior Camp, Kanawana, was open from June 26 to 

August 24, and proved to be a record season, 223 different boys 
attending, with an average daily attendance of 66. Mr. John Mac- 

Kinnon, Boys’ Work Secretary of Central, was in charge until 
August 3, Mr. G. D. Brandon relieving him until August 17, 
Mr. MacKinnon again taking charge until the close of Camp on 
August 24. The financial statement of the Junior Camp shows a 
credit balance of $302 after the season’s operations. 

The Permanent Camp Committee have seriously considered 
improvements to the buildings of the different Camps, which they 
believe to be necessary, and have asked the Finance Committee of 
the Board, who have agreed, to place in the budget this year a small 
sum to provide for needed repairs. 

Your Directors realize that the Junior Camp affords splendid 
opportunities for influencing the lives of our younger members and 
getting our-Secretaries in closest relationship possible with the boys.

Increase over last year, 1,423 members. 

Great credit is due Railroad Branch, Point St. Charles, for their 
magnificent membership drive, which lasted one week in April. 
Their objective was 200 new members, and they secured 1,199, 
bringing the membership of that branch up to 1,350. The Board of 
Management and the Secretaries of Railroad Association deserve 
our sincere congratulations. 


STAFF CHANGES. 

Central—On March 31, Mr. W. A. MacLaren resigned as 
Membership Secretary, to become General Secretary of the Quebec 
City Association. He was succeeded by Mr. David M. Watson. 

Mr. G. D. Brandon resigned as Physical Director of Boys’ Work 
to become Community Secretary at Point St. Charles and Verdun 
on May |. 

Westmount—Mr. Cecil L. Brown became Secretary of this 
Branch in February of this year. Mr. E. M. Crawford, on February 
24, became Boys’ Work Secretary, replacing Mr. C. L. Brown. 

North Branch—Mr. James McLean resigned as Assistant Secre- 
tary on February 15, and was succeeded by Mr. L. W. Clarke. 
Mr. R. P. Thomas became Physical Director, and Mr. J. G. Cruick- 
shank, Boys’ Secretary, joining the staff on May 1, 1918. 

Railroad—Mr. J. S. Teet, of Chapleau, accepted the Secretary- 
ship in November, and Mr. E. T. Armitage became Boys’ Work 
Secretary on December 18, 1918. 


CoNFERENCES. 

Your Acting General Secretary attended the following conferences 
during the year: 

Springheld, Mass——Employed Officers’ Conference, meeting over 
800 Association men, where the work of the Association in all its 
departments was considered. 

Atlantic City—Home Work General Secretaries’ Conference, 
meeting 150 invited outstanding leaders in our Movement, led by 
Dr. John R. Mott. to consider and plan the larger programme of the 
Association for after-war conditions, as to how we can meet the 
tremendous challenge and opportunity of the future in the light. of 
the great war. 


6 MONTREAL WRN 


Hamilton, Ont—The National Council Annual Meeting, where 
the entire Canadian work was reviewed and the Budget for the year 
considered and _ passed. 

These Conferences have been of the greatest benefit and have 
aided materially in planning and carrying through the year’s Asso- 
ciation work. 

Your Directors wish to express their appreciation of the splendid 
leadership and assistance given by the Board of Management, the 
Ladies’ Auxiliary, the volunteer workers, and the employed officers 
of each branch; also the Military Committee of the Red Triangle 
Hut, the Secretaries in charge, and the splendid self-sacrifice of the 
Ladies’ Military Committee under Mrs. Jas. N. Laing. 

We are glad, also, to report the most cordial relationship between 
the different denominations and the Association. The watchword of 
each is ‘‘co-operation in the extension of the Kingdom of Jesus Christ” 
in this great reconstruction period upon which we have entered, all 
realizing that earnestness of purpose and clearness of vision, coupled 
with divine leadership, shall constructively touch a large number of 
men and boys, and together we shall build up Christian character 
and good citizenship, making a progressive and happy people. 

We would bring to the attention of our leading Association 
supporters, and urge as many as possible to attend, the Convention 
called by the Canadian National Council of the Y.M.C.A., to be held 
in Winnipeg in October of this year, at which many changes in the 
programme and policies of the Association, as recommended by our 
Overseas’ Secretaries, will be considered. 


RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE CoMING YEAR. 


1. That we earnestly push a definite industrial programme, 
interviewing our large industries and securing their co-operation. 


2. That we definitely aim to bring our educational programme 
and accomplishments up to the requirements of the unmet educa- 
tional needs of men and boys. 


3. That we prayerfully and earnestly increase our religious work, 
which last year showed an improvement over the past, that we might 
increase the volume and quality of our work and reach every man 
who may become a member of the Association as well as the men 
and boys of the community. We would strongly urge upon our 
membership that every means at our disposal be used for deepening 
our spiritual life. 

That we aim to increase our membership materially this 
year. Our buildings can accommodate fifty per cent. more members 
than we now have. 

5. That we educate our membership and plan to push very 
vigorously the foreign work of the Association, supporting our 
representative in other lands. 

May we this year undertake our tasks in a spirit of real faith in 
God, in men, and in the foundation principles of our new democracy.

MONTREAL WEN 9 


CAMP KANAWANA 


SINCE the rise of the mercury, May 19, we feel that summer 

has sent a warning once again that in a few weeks the heat 
and dust of former years will be oppressing us, and when we will 
be longing for a spot where worry, care and the turmoil of the City 
can be shaken off for a few weeks. 


To those who have never been there, let me introduce Kanawana, 
the Boys’ Y.M.C.A. summer camp, and it is a camp situated on the 
shores of a lake in the Laurentians a few miles from Piedmont on 
the C.P.R. The camp, nestling among the trees, is practically 
isolated from any nearby neighbors, and here boys are free along 
with nature to live an ideal holiday among boys. 


BOYS—LOOK AT THIS PICTURE 


The equipment is splendid. Large tents for sleeping quarters. 
An immense open air roofed dining-hall, and the pavilion for games. 


Swimming, boating and games, all under able supervision, and 
the learning of hundreds of things that boys should know, fill in the 
waking hours, while the inner boy is filled between times with the 
best of food, good and wholesome, prepared by Harry. 


Supervision is in the hands of the camp staff, headed by the 
Director, a Doctor and our Educational Supervisor. 


Any of our Boys’ Secretaries will be glad to furnish all details, 
as to cost, etc. 


Camp opens June 28th, closes August 30th, 1919.

YOUNG MEN 


It is commendable for young men to join 
in ASSOCIATION in order to become im- 
bued with the principle of good citizenship 
and by their example constitute an element 
of strength for the welfare of our Country. 


2a il: aie Oia 


established for this purpose is to be con- 
gratulated on its laudable efforts. 


It is absolutely commendable for all young 


men TO SAVE 


THE MONTREAL CITY AND 
DISTRICT SAVINGS BANK 


an important association of THRIFT es- 
tablished for the safe custody and increase 
of the Savings of the people, invites all 
young men toits counters and assures them 
of a cordial welcome, however small may be 
the savings confided to its care.

Ni, POWER,. Manager, 


Branch: Corner McGill College Avenue and 
St. Catherine Street West.
